title: Exceptional points and Jordan-chain signatures in quantum first-passage statistics
abstract: Exceptional-point signatures in first-passage observables are governed by two independent survival mechanisms: nonlinear spectral defectivity must pass from the one-record or transfer description to the physical one-level first-passage ladder, and the resulting ladder Jordan mode must have nonzero overlap with the chosen preparation and terminal observation. For finite reset-form monitored quantum systems with upward-skip-free counting, we prove the exact threshold factorization $H_N(s)=R_s^N$, identify the physical Perron branch, and derive the transfer factorization $Q_s(r)=B_s(r)(R_s-rI)$. Invertibility of the cofactor gives local equality of Smith data, whereas a singular cofactor can contribute transfer multiplicity absent from the ladder. An order-two Keldysh formula yields an independent observation gate. We then prove a fixed-reset no-go theorem: even a defective full tilted generator cannot generate a cumulative-count Jordan polynomial when the post-count ladder is scalar. Finally, we construct a three-reset monitored-Lindblad witness, minimal within irreducible nonnegative ladders, with a genuine subleading $Nλ^N$ threshold term and a coherence-tuned model in which a binary terminal effect retains the exact polynomial signature at a transversal transform-domain exceptional point. The analysis is formulated at the level of exact transform-domain structure; time-domain asymptotics and perturbative robustness remain separate questions.
summary: This theoretical paper rigorously analyzes how spectral singularities, or exceptional points, manifest in the statistics of first-passage times for open quantum systems. Using advanced transform-domain techniques, the authors derive exact factorization theorems and establish fundamental no-go theorems regarding the relationship between generator defectivity and observable Jordan polynomial signatures. It provides a powerful mathematical framework for understanding measurement-induced spectral properties.
main_problem: The paper investigates the mathematical conditions under which exceptional point signatures, arising from nonlinear spectral defectivity, survive and manifest in physical quantum first-passage time statistics.
main_result: The authors establish exact threshold factorizations ($H_N(s) = R_N^s$) and prove a fixed-reset no-go theorem, showing that defective generators do not necessarily yield defective cumulative-count Jordan polynomials.
method: The analysis is highly mathematical, utilizing exact transform-domain structure (Laplace/z-transforms), spectral theory for analytic matrix pencils, and renewal theory applied to monitored quantum processes.
model_or_system: The study concerns open quantum systems monitored via quantum jumps, specifically focusing on finite reset-form monitored systems with upward-skip-free counting processes.
key_observables: Quantum first-passage-time distributions, threshold ladders ($R_s$), transfer factorizations ($Q_s(r)$), and the detection of Jordan-chain signatures (polynomial factors like $N\lambda^N$).
important_parameters: The analysis depends on the system being within the finite reset-form monitored-quantum and finite upward-skip-free matrix-renewal class.
main_assumptions: The analysis is formulated at the level of exact transform-domain structure, explicitly separating this from time-domain asymptotics and perturbative robustness.
paper_structure: The paper builds from analyzing the survival of defectivity from the transfer pencil to the physical ladder, deriving exact factorization theorems, proving the no-go theorem for defective generators, and concluding with the construction of a minimal witness model.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical tools for characterizing non-Hermitian spectral singularities (exceptional points) in the context of open quantum dynamics, which is crucial for understanding measurement back-action and quantum control.
